I had 500 user IDs to fetch. So I did arr.map(fetch) + Promise.all.

The API rate-limited me into oblivion in about 2 seconds.

Here's how to run async tasks in parallel WITHOUT blowing past the limit (thread):

1/ The trap

arr.map(asyncFn) calls the function for every item in the same tick. All the work starts at once.

5 items? Fine.
500 items? 500 simultaneous requests -> 429 Too Many Requests.

2/ Two naive fixes, both wrong

Promise.all: fast, but ignores the rate limit.
await in a for loop: safe, but painfully slow. If the API allows 5 in flight and you do 1, you waste 80% of your throughput.

We want the middle path: bounded concurrency.

4/ The better version: a worker pool

Start `size` tasks. When ANY task finishes, that slot grabs the next item immediately.

Key move: write results[index] = value (not push) so order survives out-of-order completion. Keep a `settled` flag to fail fast on the first error.

5/ Same fail-fast contract as Promise.all: first rejection wins, and no new tasks start after it.

Chunk if task durations are similar. Use a worker pool when they vary (network calls always do).

Full build + tests: https://blog.sandeepallala.com/blog/implementing-map-async-limit-javascript-utility-function
